Name: Quantifying
Description: Nanopores have emerged as a powerful tool for single-molecule sensing and sequencing. In a typical nanopore experiment, a charged analyte such as DNA is driven through the pore by an electrophoretic force generated by the applied electric field. This can be problematic, however, when analytes such as proteins carry mixed charges. An alternative driving force can be from electro-osmotic flow (EOF), the water flow that arises from an asymmetric migration of cations and anions through the nanopore.
